Ad ARPDAU is rising: The top performers climbed 54%.
Tomas Hubka
Last updated: Nov 16, 2026
min read
Ad revenue per DAU is up at every tier of the mobile market in 2026, with the top performers climbing fastest. Here’s what’s driving it.
Across the four monetization metrics on our
Benchmarks Hub
, where most metrics are not subject to fluctuation, one stands out for clearly rising through 2026. Ad revenue per daily active user has moved upward at every percentile tier we track, and the top of the market is pulling away from the rest.
What the GameAnalytics Benchmarks Hub shows
Three numbers to look at: Over the 12 months of data currently on the Hub, median Ad ARPDAU has climbed from $0.029 to $0.032, up roughly 10%. At the 75th percentile, the rise is sharper, from $0.089 to $0.111, up about 25%. And at the 95th percentile, it has climbed from $0.208 to $0.321, a 54% increase in a single year.
The gains concentrate at the top. The top 5% of games are expanding their ad revenue per player much faster than the median. Whatever is working at the top of the market isn’t trickling down evenly, and the spread between typical and strong is widening.

Independent sources confirm the trajectory. Adjust’s
2026 Mobile App Trends report
shows average CPM across mobile game genres grew from $3.63 to $4.34 in 2025, a 20% year-over-year increase. The underlying ad economics are strengthening across the board, which is consistent with the ARPDAU gains we see in our own data.
Sensor Tower’s
Mobile Game Ad Monetization 2026 report
tracks the structural shift behind the economics. The share of games using ad monetization has grown from 45% in mid-2021 to 56% in May 2026. Ad-supported titles now represent 84% of mobile game downloads. The industry isn’t just getting more ad revenue per player, but it’s running more games with ad revenue in the mix.
The pattern across these three sources points to the same thing: ad monetization is growing in revenue per player, adoption, and is increasingly central to how mobile games make money.
Where the gains are concentrating
The 54% climb at the 95th percentile is the headline number, but it’s worth asking what’s driving it. The answer sits in the format shift that defined mobile gaming in 2025 and 2026.
Game Growth Advisor’s hybrid monetization guide
estimates that around 72% of mobile developers have adopted or plan to adopt hybrid monetization, which combines in-app purchases with ad revenue in the same game rather than treating them as alternatives. Rewarded video drives about 62% of ad revenue in that model, with engagement rates of 45-60%. Hybrid casual, the category that defines this approach,
grew IAP revenue 20% in 2025 and another 23% in H1 2026
and was the only casual segment growing revenue in both periods.
The games pulling ahead on Ad ARPDAU are almost certainly the ones executing hybrid monetization well. Rewarded video opt-ins at scale, strategic ad placement that doesn’t suppress IAP conversion, and better mediation across networks all compound into the kind of 50%+ year-over-year gains we’re seeing at the top of the market.
Why this fits the engagement shift
In our
previous piece on mobile playtime
, we showed that mobile sessions have gotten shorter while session frequency has held steady. Players aren’t opening games less often, they’re staying shorter per visit.
That’s the engagement shape where ad monetization should do well. Ad impressions scale with how often a game is opened rather than how long each sitting lasts, so stable session frequency means stable impression opportunity per DAU. Shorter sessions don’t erode ad revenue the way they would erode IAP revenue, where conversion often depends on extended engagement with a game’s economy. The two findings are internally consistent: engagement thinned per visit but held at the daily level, and ad monetization grew into exactly that shape.
